title: Reading pathways
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:13Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-20T12:25:42Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No bank point teaches that different text forms are read along different paths (line by line, scanning, panel by panel); the closest, 'How technology changes reading', covers only digital-text features and is narrower and related rather than the same idea.

draft.title: Reading pathways
card: A reading pathway is the route a reader's eyes and mind take through a text. Different kinds of text are read along different paths.
read line by line, from the start to the end, so the story builds in order.
read by scanning headings, images and links, then jumping to the part that matches what the reader wants.
read panel by panel, taking in the pictures and the words in each panel before moving on.
draft.remember: Spotting how a text is meant to be read helps you work out its form and purpose.

a.q: Which description best matches how a reader moves through a web page?
opts: Scanning headings and links, then jumping to a section
Reading every sentence in order from first to last
Following the pictures one panel at a time
Reading the last paragraph first, then going back
a.why: A web page is built for scanning, so readers use headings and links to jump to what they need. Reading every sentence in order is the path for a novel, not a web page.
a.clue: Think about how you look for one fact online.

b.q: Sam opens a book and sees a page split into boxes. Each box has a drawing and a short speech bubble. Which pathway should Sam use?
opts: Panel by panel, reading the picture and words in each box
Line by line, ignoring the drawings until the end
Scanning for headings, then clicking on links
Jumping straight to the last box to find the ending
b.why: Boxes holding a drawing and speech bubble are panels, which suggests a graphic novel. It is read panel by panel. Line by line suits a novel, where the story is told in running text.
b.clue: What are the boxes on the page called?

a.best: Scanning headings and links, then jumping to a section

b.best: Panel by panel, reading the picture and words in each box
